newsitem.title: USA: CBOT old crop soymeal ends limit up, soyoil mixed.
newsitem.headline: CBOT old crop soymeal ends limit up, soyoil mixed.

text.p: CBOT old crop soymeal futures ended up the $10 per ton limit on Wednesday, lifted by aggressive commercial buying amid persistent rumors of export business, pit sources said.
Soyoil ended mixed with nearbys down on commercial selling and deferreds up on aggressive fund buying totalling at least 2,200 lots in the December.

"We saw the August meal closing the limit," said Bob Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer. "It had been about $60 down in a two week span $60 and that had reignited some interest overseas in the meal as well."
Asian traders early Wednesday said Chinese companies had been buying significant quantities of U.S. soymeal since early July as world prices slumped.
The traders said China may have bought anywhere from 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes.
New crop months posted more modest gains, limited by prospects for a bumper U.S. soybean crop this fall. Weather patterns remain conducive for crop growth, traders said.
Soymeal ended $10.20 to $5.30 per ton higher with August up $10.00 at $243.80. Soyoil closed down 0.09 cent per lb to up 0.03 cent with August down 0.03 at 22.19 cents.
Trade sources also pointed to position squaring ahead of Thursday's USDA export sales report and Friday's supply and demand data.

On the day, commercials were again aggressive buyers of old crop soymeal. Cargill Inc bought 600 lots August soymeal in opening trade, Produce Grain bought 400 August and ADM bought 200 August, pit sources said.
Cargill Investor Services and E.D. and F. Man International were also said to be buyers of the August.
In soyoil, two large-scale buyers propped up new crop months. Prudential Securities bought 1,000 lots December and R.J. O'Brien bought 1,200 December, traders said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 38,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 32,502 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 28,000 lots, against Tuesday's 19,002.
